cases.exposure_context_quote: A 48-year-old male was brought to casualty after consuming poison accompanied by the consumption of alcohol. The patient was an occasional alcoholic.
cases.agent: UNVERIFIED (specific agent not named; intermediate syndrome indicates an organophosphate pesticide: title 'Intermediate Syndrome Secondary to Organophosphate Poisoning')

symptoms.finding: unconsciousness with frothing from mouth, decreased responsiveness
symptoms.quote: He was found unconscious and had frothing from the mouth, decreased responsiveness
difficulty in breathing, and unstable vitals with a blood pressure of 100/60 mmHg, pulse rate of 102 per minute, and oxygen saturation of 75%. Auscultation revealed bilateral coarse crepitations.

symptoms.finding: intermediate syndrome with respiratory muscle weakness requiring reintubation (worsened 4 days after initial extubation)
symptoms.quote: However, due to worsening conditions, the patient was reintubated four days later, accompanied by the presence of secretions and reduced air entry.

symptoms.finding: bilateral loculated pleural effusions with subsegmental atelectasis
symptoms.quote: Thoracic ultrasound showed bilateral pleural effusion, with 260 cc on the left and 80 cc on the right, accompanied by subsegmental atelectasis.

cases.time_to_care: UNVERIFIED (no interval between ingestion and casualty arrival stated)

treatment.name: atropine 2 mg
treatment.quote: medical management was started with atropine 2 mg, injection of midazolam 2 mg IV, succinylcholine 75 mg IV, and intravenous fluids.

treatment.name: intubation and mechanical ventilation (volume control, FiO2 100%)
treatment.quote: An endotracheal tube was connected to a mechanical ventilator set to volume control mode with a fraction of inspired oxygen at 100%.

treatment.name: intravenous fluids

treatment.name: structured physiotherapy program for 2 weeks (patient education, secretion mobilization, incentive spirometry, chest expansion exercises, positioning, mobilization)
treatment.quote: Physiotherapy interventions included patient education, secretion mobilization, vital capacity improvement, secondary complication prevention, chest expansion exercises, dyspnea-relieving positions, and mobilization.

cases.outcome: significant improvement in functional independence, mobility and psychological well-being over 2 weeks of physiotherapy (progressed from maximal assistance to no assistance / walking without assistance); final discharge status UNVERIFIED
cases.outcome_quote: Significant improvements in functional independence, mobility, and psychological well-being were observed throughout the intervention period.
cases.sequelae: intermediate syndrome with respiratory muscle weakness; bilateral pleural effusions (severity/improvement documented on day-1 and day-7 chest X-rays)
cases.notes: Physiotherapy-focused case report; toxicologic details (specific agent, dose, time to care, pralidoxime use) not provided.
